text:
The issue is that when `Progress` is disabled, it still outputs a blank line on non-interactive consoles. This happens in the `stop()` method when `self.console.print()` is called, even if the progress was never displayed.

I have updated the `stop()` method to check `self.disable` before printing, ensuring no output occurs if the progress was disabled from the start.

I also reviewed the `start()` method, which already contains a check for `self.disable` and does not require modification to prevent output when disabled.

The fix is applied to `rich/progress.py`.

    "new_string": "        if not self.disable and not self.console.is_interactive and not self.console.is_jupyter:\n            self.console.print()\n",
